sources.title: Radio communications aboard the ISS
sources.values_read: NASA astronaut Jonny Kim uses a ham radio to speak with students from the International Space Station. This is ISS communications, not a Mars control room.
sources.supports: Factual cassette photograph and visible credit only; no game repair procedure.
sources.note: NASA. Image iss073e0252501. Selected the ham-radio photograph in the article, not its Cupola hero photograph or author avatar.

sources.title: ISS solar arrays above Earth
sources.values_read: Solar arrays on the Russian segment of the International Space Station, photographed by an Expedition 38 crew member on February 5, 2014. Earth is visible beyond the station.
sources.supports: Factual cassette photograph and visible credit only; no game repair procedure.
sources.note: NASA. Image ISS038-E-042665. Replaced the appendix's ESA/NASA-credited solar-array image with this NASA-credited ISS photograph to avoid assuming NASA guidance also licenses a partner's photograph.

sources.title: Radishes in the ISS Advanced Plant Habitat
sources.values_read: Radishes growing in the Plant Habitat-02 experiment aboard the International Space Station, photographed on November 11, 2020. The chamber supports controlled plant-growth research.
sources.supports: Factual cassette photograph and visible credit only; no game repair procedure.
sources.note: NASA/Kate Rubins. Image iss064e004220. Appendix candidate retained; the photograph shows plants and habitat equipment.

sources.title: Advanced Plant Habitat ground development unit
sources.values_read: A NASA Advanced Plant Habitat engineering development unit at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, 2016. This photographed ground prototype is an engineering analogy, not a Martian garden dome.
sources.supports: Factual cassette photograph and visible credit only; no game repair procedure.
sources.note: NASA/Bill White. Image 30795688500_ed64d9f74b_o. Appendix candidate retained and explicitly labeled as an Earth ground project.

sources.title: Ultrasound research in the ISS Columbus laboratory
sources.values_read: NASA astronaut Chris Cassidy performs an ultrasound on ESA astronaut Luca Parmitano in the ISS Columbus laboratory on August 21, 2013. This is medical research, not a game reagent recipe.
sources.supports: Factual cassette photograph and visible credit only; no game repair procedure.
sources.note: NASA. Image ISS036-E-035750. Appendix candidate retained; image identity verified against the official caption.

sources.title: Spacesuit and tool preparation in Quest
sources.values_read: NASA astronaut Michael Hopkins prepares tools and U.S. spacesuits inside the ISS Quest airlock on December 17, 2020. This is real ISS suit staging, not a fictional Mars leak repair.
sources.supports: Factual cassette photograph and visible credit only; no game repair procedure.
sources.note: NASA. Image iss064e013338. Appendix candidate retained; image identity verified against the official caption.
